mainTopic: Partitions and the form of a doorway (צורת הפתח) for כלאים and שבת, and the opening of the משנה on how to make a מבוי fit for carrying.
overview: The amud opens with a dispute about whether a braid of vines (פֵּיאָה) between poles counts as a partition for כלאים and for שבת. The גמרא reconciles רבי יוחנן's two statements by the distance between the poles: a braid attached from the side works for כלאים at ten אמות but not at more than ten. It proves this distinction from a story about רבי יוחנן בן נורי. Next it turns to רב חסדא's rules for a צורת הפתח: it is worthless if made from the side, and it must be strong enough to hold even a straw door. ריש לקיש adds that it needs a hinge marker, while רב אשי apparently required nothing extra. רב נחמן and רב ששת argue over whether the side reeds must touch the top reed. Each acts on his view in the house of the ריש גלותא, and an arch ברייתא about מזוזה, explained by אביי, ends up working against רב ששת. Then a new משנה brings the dispute between בית שמאי, בית הלל and רבי אליעזר over what makes a מבוי fit for carrying. The גמרא limits the משנה to a closed alley and shows that the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל do not prove the Torah minimum of walls. It then asks whether רבי אליעזר's two side posts also require a קורה, a question whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute about a braid of vines as a partition
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting his teacher, says a פֵּיאָה works as a partition for כלאים but not for שבת. רבי יוחנן says it works for neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: A braid of vines is permitted regarding כלאים, but not regarding שבת. And רבי יוחנן said: just as it is not a partition for שבת, so too it is not a partition for כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a dispute about whether a braid of vines strung between poles counts as a partition. The first opinion (ריש לקיש in the name of his teacher) says it works only for כלאים, and רבי יוחנן says it works for neither.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partition does different jobs in different areas of הלכה. For כלאים it separates a vineyard from other crops so they may be planted close together. For שבת it can turn an area into a private domain. The first opinion treats כלאים as more lenient than שבת, while רבי יוחנן holds the braid fails in both areas.

keyTerms.meaning: A braid of vines plaited around poles, used like a partition
The prohibition of planting different species (here, grapevines and other crops) together
Partitions or walls that halachically separate areas
Permitted, meaning here that it works as a valid partition

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-quote. The first statement belongs to ריש לקיש, who is quoting his teacher רבי יהודה בר רבי חנינא, even though the name does not appear next. You need to know this for the next step.

phrases.english: A braid of vines is permitted with regard to diverse kinds,
phrases.notes: It counts as a partition for כלאים.

phrases.english: but not with regard to Shabbat.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Just as it is not a partition for Shabbat,
so too it is not a partition for diverse kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a dispute quoted on the previous amud. It is set up to clash with an earlier dispute between the same אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: a braid of vines is a partition for כלאים only. רבי יוחנן: it is a partition for neither כלאים nor שבת.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's two statements do not contradict
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's two rulings are reconciled. One is his own opinion and the other is his teacher's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable that ריש לקיש's statement against ריש לקיש's other statement is no difficulty: this one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that ריש לקיש seems to contradict himself, then immediately solves it. In one place he gave his own opinion, and here he was only reporting his teacher's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier dispute, ריש לקיש held that the braid works even for שבת. Here he says it does not work for שבת. There is no real conflict, because the stricter ruling here is his teacher רבי יהודה בר רבי חנינא's view, not his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it is understandable. Introduces the part that works before raising a problem
It is not a difficulty
His own (opinion)
Of his teacher

phrases.english: Granted, Reish Lakish against Reish Lakish
phrases.notes: His statement here seems to clash with what he said in the earlier dispute.

phrases.english: is not a difficulty:
this one is his own view,
that one is his teacher's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares step 1 with the earlier dispute and settles the apparent contradiction for ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the two statements come from different people (student vs. teacher).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש seems to hold both that the braid works for שבת and that it does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: His own view is that it works even for שבת. The stricter ruling is only a report of his teacher's view.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's two statements do contradict
steps.stepSummary: Unlike ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן's contradiction cannot be explained as quoting a teacher, so it remains a real difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן's statement against רבי יוחנן's other statement is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now raises the real problem. רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself, and there is no easy way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier dispute, רבי יוחנן held that the braid does work for כלאים. Here he says it works for neither כלאים nor שבת. Both statements are said in his own name, so the student-versus-teacher answer from step 2 cannot help.

keyTerms.meaning: But / however. Turns to the part that is still a problem
A difficulty / contradiction

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan against Rabbi Yochanan
is a difficulty!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא structure. ריש לקיש was resolved, but רבי יוחנן is not.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's consistency on whether a braid of vines works as a partition for כלאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Earlier he said it works for כלאים. Here he says it does not. Both are his own opinion, so they clash.

steps.title: The problem is sharpened: what if both cases are from the side?
steps.stepSummary: A distinction between vines placed on top of the poles and vines attached from the side would solve the problem. But if both cases are from the side, what can be said?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well if you say that there the vines were on top of the poles and here they were attached from the side. But if you say both cases are from the side, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible way out (on top vs. from the side), then blocks it by asking what happens if both cases are from the side. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vines laid on top of the poles look like a real doorway frame, while vines tied on the side are weaker. That difference could explain why רבי יוחנן ruled differently in the two places. But if both cases involve vines tied from the side, this distinction disappears and the contradiction is back.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
On top of them (the poles)
From the side
Fine / it works out well
What is there to say? (What answer is left?)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say:
there, the vines were on top of the poles,
here, they were from the side, it works well.
But if you say:
both this and that are from the side,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a possible answer to step 3 and shows why it may not be enough, which keeps the difficulty alive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to reconcile רבי יוחנן's statements by the position of the vines.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'on top vs. side' answer only works if the cases really differ that way. If both are from the side, the distinction fails.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. The 'on top vs. side' idea is raised only to show it may not cover every case, so the real answer is still coming.

steps.title: The answer: ten אמות versus more than ten
steps.stepSummary: Both cases are from the side. Where the poles are ten אמות apart the braid works for כלאים, and where they are more than ten apart it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, both cases are from the side. There the gap is ten אמות, and here the gap is more than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבי יוחנן's contradiction. It agrees both cases are from the side, but says they differ in how wide the gap between the poles is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of up to ten אמות can be treated as an opening (like a doorway) within a partition. A wider gap is too big to count as a doorway. So רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling for כלאים applies to a ten-אמה gap, and his strict ruling applies to a gap wider than ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth. Introduces the real answer while keeping the earlier assumption
Both this and that
With (a gap of) ten אמות
With (a gap of) more than ten אמות

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן is consistent. A braid of vines tied from the side counts as a partition for כלאים when the poles are ten אמות apart, but not when they are more than ten apart.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the gap size of ten אמות is the dividing line for whether an opening still counts as part of a partition. This idea recurs throughout the laws of מחיצות.

phrases.english: Actually, both this and that are from the side:
there, with a gap of ten cubits,
here, with a gap of more than ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sharpened difficulty of step 4 by finding a new difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the cases differ in the width of the gap between the poles.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If both cases are from the side, רבי יוחנן's statements seem to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gap of ten אמות makes the braid valid for כלאים. A gap of more than ten makes it invalid even for כלאים.

steps.title: Where do we see the line between ten and more than ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the law changes between ten אמות and more than ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know that we make a difference between ten and more than ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in Step 5 depended on a rule that ten אמות is different from more than ten. Now the גמרא asks where that rule comes from. This line sets up the next move, where the source is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 solved רבי יוחנן's contradiction by assuming that side-attached braids depend on the distance between the poles. An answer is only as strong as its basis, so the גמרא wants a source. Nothing is challenged yet. It is just a request for support.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say it? A request for a source.
There is a difference for us. We distinguish between cases.
More than ten (אמות)

phrases.english: And from where do you say

phrases.aramaic: דְּשָׁנֵי לַן בֵּין עֶשֶׂר לְיוֹתֵר מֵעֶשֶׂר
phrases.english: that we distinguish between ten and more than ten?
phrases.notes: This refers to the distance in אמות between the poles or trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the distinction that Step 5's answer depended on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a side-attached partition is judged differently at ten אמות than at more than ten.

steps.title: The story of רבי יהושע and רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells ריש לקיש the true version of a story. רבי יוחנן בן נורי ruled that sowing beside a vine stretched between trees is permitted at ten אמות and forbidden at more than ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: That is not how the story happened. רבי יהושע went to רבי יוחנן בן נורי to learn Torah, even though he was already an expert in the laws of כלאים. He found him sitting among the trees, and he stretched a vine from one tree to another. He said to him: רבי, if there are grapevines here, may one sow seeds over here? He answered: at ten it is permitted, at more than ten it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as the source. רבי יוחנן בן נורי gave a ruling that changes at exactly ten אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vine was stretched between trees to act as a partition between grapevines on one side and seeds on the other. רבי יוחנן בן נורי's answer separates ten from more than ten, which is the same line used in Step 5. But we don't yet know whether the vine was on top of the trees or on their side. The next step works that out.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not how the incident happened. It corrects someone else's version of a story.
An expert, well-versed
A vine branch
Trees
To sow (seeds)

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling 'ten is permitted' is NOT about the size of the vineyard. It is about the distance between the two trees that hold up the stretched vine.

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Reish Lakish:
That is not how the incident happened,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש had told this story a different way.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָלַךְ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֵצֶל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yehoshua went to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri
to learn Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּקִי בְּהִלְכוֹת כִּלְאַיִם,
phrases.english: even though he was an expert in the laws of diverse kinds,
and he found him sitting among the trees
and he stretched a vine branch from tree to tree.
phrases.notes: The one stretching the branch here is רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: And he said to him: Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: אִי גְּפָנִים כָּאן מַהוּ לִזְרוֹעַ כָּאן?
phrases.english: if there are grapevines here, may one sow here?
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is one side of the stretched vine. The second 'here' is the other side.

phrases.english: He said to him: at ten, it is permitted;
at more than ten, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by bringing a source story.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a partition for כלאים works at ten אמות but not at more than ten
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling to רבי יהושע, as reported by רבי יוחנן

steps.title: The story can't be about vines placed on top
steps.stepSummary: If the vine was on top of the trees, the 'forbidden beyond ten' ruling would contradict a ברייתא that permits a top braid even beyond ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say the vine was on top of the trees, would more than ten really be forbidden? But a ברייתא teaches: if there were forked reeds and he made a braid on top of them, it is permitted even beyond ten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests which case the story is about. It shows that the 'on top' reading does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא says that a braid laid on top of forked reeds is a valid partition for כלאים at any distance. So if the story were about a vine on top, forbidding it beyond ten would clash with that ברייתא. The 'on top' reading is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
On top of them
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Forked reeds, poles with a fork at the top
From above, on top

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If you say the vine was on top of them,
would more than ten be forbidden?
But it was taught: if there were forked reeds there
and he made a braid for them on top,
even at more than ten, it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case in the story by ruling out the 'on top' reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling as being about a vine placed on top of the trees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits a top braid even beyond ten, so 'forbidden beyond ten' cannot be about a top braid.

steps.title: So the story is about the side, and the distinction is proven
steps.stepSummary: The story must be about a vine attached from the side. That proves a side partition works for כלאים at ten but not beyond ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about a vine on the side, and he told him: at ten it is permitted, at more than ten it is forbidden? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'on top' reading failed, the story must be about a side-attached vine. The proof is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reading left is the side case. So רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling tells us that a side-attached vine works up to ten אמות and fails beyond. That is exactly the rule Step 5 needed, so Step 5's answer to רבי יוחנן's contradiction now stands on solid ground.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it? This introduces the only reading left.
From the side
Learn from it. The proof is accepted.

steps.whatToRemember: A braid on top works for כלאים at any distance. A braid attached from the side works for כלאים only when the poles are ten אמות apart or less. This is what settles רבי יוחנן's two statements.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about the side,
and he was telling him: at ten, it is permitted;
more than ten, it is forbidden.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 8's elimination of the 'on top' reading to conclude that the story is about the side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A side-attached partition works for כלאים at ten אמות and not beyond, which confirms Step 5's answer.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a צורת הפתח made from the side is worthless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב חסדא's statement itself: a צורת הפתח with the crossbeam placed at the side of the posts accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב חסדא said: if someone made a צורת הפתח from the side, he has done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to study רב חסדא's statement, which was mentioned earlier in the sugya. This opens a new discussion of that statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper צורת הפתח needs two posts with a crossbeam resting on top of them. If the crossbeam is attached to the side of the posts instead, רב חסדא says it does not count at all. The גמרא will now discuss this ruling on its own terms.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier.
Form of a doorway: two posts with a beam across the top
He has done nothing at all.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the הלכות. רב חסדא is talking about a צורת הפתח, which is invalid when made from the side. The ruling just proven (side braid works up to ten אמות) was about a פֵּיאָה for כלאים.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Ḥisda said:
A form of a doorway that one made from the side,
he has not done anything at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the side discussion and returns to רב חסדא's statement, which was quoted earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת הפתח whose crossbeam is attached at the side of the posts, not on top, is completely invalid.

steps.title: A doorway form must be strong enough to hold a door
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a צורת הפתח must be sturdy enough to support a door, even if it is only a door made of straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: The צורת הפתח the Sages spoke about must be strong enough that a door could be set up in it, even a door made of straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second rule from רב חסדא about how a צורת הפתח must be built: it must be strong enough to hold a door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צורת הפתח works because it looks like a real doorway, so it must be able to work like one. It does not need to hold a heavy wooden door. It only needs to hold a light door made of straw.

keyTerms.meaning: Strong, sturdy
To set up a door in it
A door made of straw, a very light door

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
The form of a doorway that the Sages spoke of
must be strong
enough to set up a door in it
and even a door made of straw.
phrases.notes: The standard is low. Only a flimsy door needs to be supported.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate statement of רב חסדא about צורת הפתח, following his first one in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת הפתח must be sturdy enough to hold at least a straw door.

steps.title: A doorway form needs a marker for hinges
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי ינאי, rules that a צורת הפתח needs a היכר ציר, a visible place for hinges.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: A צורת הפתח needs a marker for hinges.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a further requirement: the doorway form needs a sign showing where hinges would go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא required strength. Here ריש לקיש adds something different: the structure must show that a door could actually hang there. This makes it look even more like a real doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: A marker or sign for a hinge
Hinge, the pivot on which a door turns
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
The form of a doorway requires a marker for hinges.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another construction requirement for צורת הפתח after רב חסדא's strength requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת הפתח requires a היכר ציר.

steps.title: What is a hinge marker?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly a היכר ציר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a marker for hinges?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term ריש לקיש just used. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The term היכר ציר is unclear. Does it mean a real hinge, or only a sign of one? The גמרא wants the exact physical meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?

phrases.english: What is a marker for hinges?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term from Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical definition of היכר ציר.

steps.title: רב אויא explains: loops
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא explains that a היכר ציר means loops into which a hinge could be inserted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said: Loops.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא answers the question. The hinge marker is a set of loops on the doorpost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full hinge is not needed. Small loops that a hinge could fit into are enough to show that a door could hang there.

keyTerms.meaning: Loops or rings into which a hinge is inserted

phrases.english: Rav Avya said: Loops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: היכר ציר means loops (אבקתא) on the post for a hinge.

steps.title: רב אחא asks what רב אשי taught
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא, son of רב אויא, meets רב אשי's students and asks whether their teacher said anything about צורת הפתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רב אויא found the students of רב אשי. He said to them: Did the Master say anything about צורת הפתח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. The son of רב אויא, who explained the loops, wants to know רב אשי's view. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His father had just defined the hinge marker. Now the son checks whether רב אשי agreed that such a marker is required.

keyTerms.meaning: He found them
The Master, a respectful way to refer to a teacher
Anything

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha, the son of Rav Avya, found
the students of Rav Ashi, and said to them:
Did the Master say anything about the form of a doorway?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְתַלְמִידֵי דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the hinge-marker topic through a story checking רב אשי's position.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב אשי taught any requirement, such as a היכר ציר, for a צורת הפתח.

steps.title: רב אשי said nothing about it
steps.stepSummary: The students answer that רב אשי said nothing at all, which implies he did not require a hinge marker.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He said nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's students answer that their teacher added no requirement. This suggests a hinge marker is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, 'he said nothing' does not mean רב אשי was silent on the topic. It means he did not demand any extra feature like loops. So רב אשי seems to disagree with ריש לקיש's requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing at all, meaning he required nothing extra

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'he said nothing' as just a missing tradition. It tells us something: רב אשי did not require a היכר ציר.

phrases.english: They said to him:
He said nothing at all.
phrases.notes: That means no hinge marker is needed at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: לֹא אָמַר וְלֹא כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question from Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי did not require a היכר ציר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a disagreement about whether a צורת הפתח needs a hinge marker at all.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the basic doorway shape
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a צורת הפתח is made of one reed on each side and one reed across the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: The צורת הפתח the Sages spoke about is a reed on this side, a reed on that side, and a reed on top of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא giving the basic structure of a צורת הפתח. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thin reeds are enough. All that is needed is two upright reeds and one reed lying across the top. The ברייתא does not say whether the pieces must touch, and that gap leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught, introducing a ברייתא
A reed
On top of them

phrases.english: It was taught: The form of a doorway that the Sages spoke of
is a reed from here and a reed from there
and a reed on top of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from extra requirements (strength, hinges) to the basic shape of a צורת הפתח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת הפתח is two side reeds and one reed on top.

steps.title: Must the side reeds touch the top reed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the side reeds must reach up and touch the top reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do they need to touch, or do they not need to touch?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a detail that the ברייתא left open. Must the upright reeds actually touch the reed on top?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top reed could be held up some other way, with a gap between it and the side reeds. The question is whether the doorway shape still counts with that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: To touch
They need to

phrases.english: Do they need to touch,
or do they not need to touch?

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכִין לִיגַּע, אוֹ אֵין צְרִיכִין לִיגַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail left open in the ברייתא of Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the side reeds must touch the top reed for the צורת הפתח to be valid.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the reeds do not need to touch, and רב ששת says they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They do not need to touch. And רב ששת said: They need to touch.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question. The גמרא records their disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, a gap between the side reeds and the top reed is fine, because it still looks like a doorway. According to רב ששת, the pieces must be connected, or it is not a real doorway frame.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who rules the reeds need not touch
אמורא who rules the reeds must touch

steps.whatToRemember: A צורת הפתח is two side reeds and a top reed. There is a dispute whether the side reeds must touch the top one: רב נחמן says no, רב ששת says yes.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֵין צְרִיכִין לִיגַּע.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: They do not need to touch.
And Rav Sheshet said: They need to touch.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֵין צְרִיכִין לִיגַּע. וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: צְרִיכִין לִיגַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: touching is not required. רב ששת: touching is required.

steps.title: רב נחמן builds a doorway-frame his own way
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן acts on his ruling in the house of the ריש גלותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן went and acted in practice in the house of the ריש גלותא, following his own ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. רב נחמן actually builds a צורת הפתח following his own opinion, so the side reeds do not touch the top reed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the argument was only words. Here רב נחמן acts on his ruling in a real, public place: the house of the ריש גלותא. This sets up רב ששת's reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a practical action; acting on a ruling in real life
the Exilarch, the leader of the Jews in Babylonia
according to his own teaching or ruling

phrases.english: Rav Nachman went and performed an action
in the house of the Exilarch, according to his own ruling.
phrases.notes: He made a doorway-frame where the side reeds did not touch the top reed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב נחמן's ruling from Step 19 put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן relied on his own view that the reeds need not touch.

steps.title: רב ששת has the reeds torn down
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells רב גדא to pull out the reeds and throw them away, and he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to his attendant רב גדא: Go, pull them out and throw them away. He went, pulled them out, and threw them away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת holds that this doorway-frame does not count. He sends his attendant to remove it, and the attendant does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רב ששת, a frame whose reeds do not touch is not a צורת הפתח at all. So carrying based on it would be forbidden. Tearing it down openly shows how strongly he holds his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: his attendant (a student who serves his teacher)
pull out
throw them away

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ רַב גַּדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to his attendant, Rav Gadda:
Go, pull them out, throw them away.
He went, pulled them out, and threw them away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ רַב גַּדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת reacts to רב נחמן's action by acting on his own opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת treats a frame with non-touching reeds as invalid.

steps.title: רב גדא is jailed and then walks free
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא's people jail רב גדא, and רב ששת calls him out of prison.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of the ריש גלותא's house found him and jailed him. רב ששת went, stood at the door, and said to him: גדא, come out, come! He came out and came.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רב גדא is punished for wrecking the frame. Then רב ששת stands at the prison door and calls him, and רב גדא simply walks out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריש גלותא's household relied on רב נחמן, so they saw the removal as destroying the צורת הפתח that let them carry. רב ששת calls his attendant out openly, and no one stops him. The story shows both sides acting firmly on their rulings, but it does not decide the law.

keyTerms.meaning: they imprisoned him
at the door/gate
go out, come (here)

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רב נחמן and רב ששת was not just theory. Each acted on his view in real life.

phrases.english: The members of the Exilarch's house found him and imprisoned him.
Rav Sheshet went and stood at the door,
and said to him: Gadda, go out, come!
He went out and came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of רב גדא's action and closes the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is given. The story shows both rulings being acted on.

steps.title: רב ששת asks רבה בר שמואל for a teaching on doorway-frames
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks רבה בר שמואל whether he learned anything about צורת הפתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת met רבה בר שמואל and said to him: Did the master learn anything about צורת הפתח?
steps.whatsHappening: A new scene begins. רב ששת looks for an older teaching (a ברייתא) about doorway-frames. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as Step 15, where רב אחא asked about רב אשי. Here רב ששת is hunting for a source that might shed light on what counts as a proper doorway shape.

keyTerms.meaning: did the master learn (teach) anything?
he found/met him

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet met Rabba bar Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תָּנֵי מָר מִידֵּי בְּצוּרַת הַפֶּתַח?
phrases.english: and said to him: Did the master learn anything about the form of a doorway?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רב נחמן–רב ששת dispute. רב ששת looks for a source on doorway-frames that bears on whether the top must touch the sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a known ברייתא dealing with צורת הפתח.

steps.title: A teaching about an arched gateway and mezuzah
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל quotes a ברייתא. For an arch, רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה and the חכמים exempt it. Everyone agrees that if its legs are ten טפחים high, it needs one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Yes, we learned: an arched gateway (כיפה) — רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה, and the חכמים exempt it. And they agree that if its legs are ten טפחים high, it requires one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל answers with a ברייתא about an arched entrance. The question is whether such an arch counts as a doorway that needs a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An arch has no separate doorposts and lintel. Its sides curve into its top. So the argument is whether a shape like that still counts as a real doorway. Both sides agree that if the straight 'legs' themselves reach ten טפחים, it is clearly a doorway and needs a מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: an arch; an arched gateway
the scroll placed on a doorpost
its legs: the straight upright sides of the arch before it starts to curve
and they agree
exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measurements. 'Legs of ten' means the straight sides alone are ten טפחים tall. The total height of the arch is a different measurement, and אביי uses it in the next steps.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, we learned:
An arched gateway — Rabbi Meir obligates it in a mezuzah,
and the Rabbis exempt it.
And they agree that if its legs are ten handbreadths high
that it is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא: for an arch, רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה and the חכמים exempt it. Everyone agrees it needs one when its legs are ten טפחים.

steps.title: אביי: the cases everyone agrees need no mezuzah
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that everyone agrees there is no obligation if the arch is ten tall with legs under three, or if the legs are three but the arch is under ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that if it is ten טפחים high but its legs are not three, or if its legs are three but it is not ten high, it is nothing (no מזוזה).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to explain the ברייתא. First he rules out two cases where both רבי מאיר and the חכמים agree there is no obligation at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doorway needs both enough straight sides (three טפחים) and enough total height (ten טפחים). If either one is missing, nobody calls it a doorway. This narrows down where the real argument must be.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees
ten טפחים tall (the full height)
it is nothing; no obligation

phrases.english: Abaye said: Everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: אִם גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה וְאֵין בְּרַגְלֶיהָ שְׁלֹשָׁה,
phrases.english: if it is ten handbreadths high but its legs are not three,
or alternatively, its legs are three
but it is not ten high — it is nothing (no obligation).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts defining the exact case of the argument in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arch missing either three טפחים of legs or ten טפחים of total height needs no מזוזה, according to everyone.

steps.title: אביי: the exact case where they argue
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about an arch with three-טפחים legs and ten טפחים of height, which is less than four wide at the ten mark but could be carved out to make four.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue when its legs are three, it is ten high, and it is not four wide, but there is room to carve it out to complete it to four.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pinpoints the argument. The arch has the needed height and legs. But at ten טפחים high it is less than four טפחים wide, though it could be carved wider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only thing missing is width at the required height, and that width could be created by carving. רבי מאיר treats the possible carving as if it were already done, so a מזוזה is required. The חכמים look only at what exists now, so it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: where they disagree
four טפחים wide
to carve out or cut away
to complete it (to the needed size)

steps.whatToRemember: Arch argument in short: legs of three and height of ten are both present. The only question is whether width that could be carved out counts as already there.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is where its legs are three
and it is ten high, but it is not four wide,
and there is room in it to carve out to complete it to four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's explanation by naming the one case in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about an arch that lacks four טפחים of width at ten טפחים high, when carving could supply it.

steps.title: The root of the arch argument: may we imagine carving to complete
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי מאיר holds חוקקין להשלים and the חכמים hold אין חוקקין להשלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds that we may carve out the arch to complete the needed width. The חכמים hold that we may not carve it out to complete the width.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his explanation. He gives the reason behind the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about the arch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the height of ten טפחים, the arch is less than four טפחים wide, but enough material is there to carve it out to four. רבי מאיר treats it as if it were already carved, so it needs a מזוזה. The חכמים look only at how it actually is now, so it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: We may carve out to complete the needed measurement. The space counts as if it were already carved.
We may not count imagined carving. Only the actual measurement counts.
An arch, here an arched gateway

steps.whatToRemember: Arch dispute: רבי מאיר says חוקקין להשלים (a מזוזה is needed). The חכמים say אין חוקקין להשלים (no מזוזה is needed). Both sides agree on the hidden point that the ceiling does not have to touch the doorposts.
steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is actually carving anything. The question is only whether we may count the space as if it had been carved.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא assumes an arched opening can count as a doorway even though its ceiling does not touch the doorposts. This works against רב ששת's view about צורת הפתח, and the next step reacts to that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: we carve out to complete [the four handbreadths],
and the Rabbis hold: we do not carve out to complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes אביי's explanation from step 26 by naming the principle the two sides argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: חוקקין להשלים. רבנן: אין חוקקין להשלים.

steps.title: רב ששת asks that the arch ברייתא not be shared
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells רבה בר שמואל not to tell the ריש גלותא's household anything from the arch ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: If you find them, do not say anything at all to the ריש גלותא's household from this ברייתא about the arch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת sees that the ברייתא goes against his own view. He asks רבה בר שמואל not to tell it to the ריש גלותא's people, who jailed רב גדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת held that in a צורת הפתח the top reed must touch the side reeds. The arch ברייתא shows that a ceiling counts even when it does not touch the doorposts. That supports the ריש גלותא's household, so רב ששת asks for silence and in effect admits the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: If you find (meet) them
The household of the Exilarch
Not anything at all

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with רב ששת quietly admitting that the ברייתא is a proof against him.

phrases.english: He [Rav Sheshet] said to him: If you find them —

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא לְהוּ לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
phrases.english: do not say to the Exilarch's household
anything at all from this baraita of the arch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת reacts to the ברייתא that רבה בר שמואל quoted and אביי explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The arch ברייתא is a real proof that the top of a doorway does not need to touch its sides, against רב ששת. He accepts this by asking that it not be told.

steps.title: New משנה: what makes a מבוי fit for carrying
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי require a לחי and a קורה. בית הלל require a לחי or a קורה. רבי אליעזר requires two לחיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How do we make an alleyway fit for carrying? בית שמאי say: a side post and a crossbeam. בית הלל say: either a side post or a crossbeam. רבי אליעזר says: two side posts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings three opinions on what is needed at the entrance of a מבוי so that people may carry inside it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי want two fixes together: a לחי on the side and a קורה above. בית הלל are satisfied with just one of them. רבי אליעזר wants a לחי on each side of the entrance. Whether he also requires a קורה is a question the גמרא raises later, in step 38.

keyTerms.meaning: Making an alleyway fit for carrying on שבת
A side post placed at the alley's entrance
A crossbeam placed across the top of the entrance
Two side posts, one on each side
Short for מתניתין, meaning 'our משנה'

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Rendering an alleyway fit [for carrying]:
Beit Shammai say: a side post and a crossbeam;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: either a side post or a crossbeam.
Rabbi Eliezer says: two side posts.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶכְשֵׁר מָבוֹי, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לֶחִי וְקוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new section. The משנה starts a fresh topic about the requirements for a מבוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: לחי וקורה. בית הלל: לחי או קורה. רבי אליעזר: two לחיין.

steps.title: A student limits the argument to wider alleys
steps.stepSummary: A student, quoting רבי ישמעאל, says that for a מבוי under four אמות wide everyone agrees one fix is enough. The argument is only about a מבוי from four to ten אמות wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ישמעאל, a student said before רבי עקיבא: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about an alley less than four אמות wide, which may be fixed with either a לחי or a קורה. What did they argue about? An alley wider than four אמות and up to ten. There בית שמאי say a לחי and a קורה, and בית הלל say either a לחי or a קורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the משנה, a student narrows the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. He says they argue only about a medium-width alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the student, even בית שמאי agree that a narrow alley (under four אמות) needs only one fix. The two-fix requirement of בית שמאי applies only to alleys between four and ten אמות wide.

keyTerms.meaning: One student
Less than four אמות wide
Becomes permitted
And up to ten (אמות)

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael, one student said before Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: about an alleyway that is less than four cubits [wide],

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא נִיתָּר אוֹ בְּלֶחִי אוֹ בְּקוֹרָה.
phrases.english: that it is permitted with either a side post or a crossbeam.
About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל רָחָב מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד עֶשֶׂר,
phrases.english: About one wider than four cubits and up to ten,
where Beit Shammai say: a side post and a crossbeam,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: either a side post or a crossbeam.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This narrows the scope of the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under four אמות: everyone agrees one fix is enough. From four to ten אמות: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: they argue about both widths
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the student's limit. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about both the narrow and the wider alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: They argued about this case and about that case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the student. He says the argument covers both narrow alleys and medium-width alleys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי עקיבא's view, בית שמאי require both a לחי and a קורה even for an alley under four אמות wide. So the argument from the start of the משנה applies to every alley up to ten אמות wide.

keyTerms.meaning: About this and about that, meaning both cases
They disagreed

steps.whatToRemember: The student says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about alleys from four to ten אמות wide. רבי עקיבא says they argue about narrow alleys too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
They disagreed about this and about that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה נֶחְלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects the student's narrowing in step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The student's claim that the argument is limited to alleys from four to ten אמות wide.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The student was wrong to say everyone agrees on alleys under four אמות. בית שמאי require two fixes there too.

steps.title: The משנה seems to match neither opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows, since it seems to fit neither חנניה nor the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose opinion is this? It is not like חנניה and not like the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out a problem. The משנה's argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל does not match either side of the earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, חנניה and the תנא קמא argue about an alley open on both ends. Both of them agree that a לחי and קורה alone are not enough there, and they want more, like a צורת הפתח or doors. The גמרא is assuming for now that the משנה speaks about every kind of alley, so the משנה looks like a third, unrelated opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
A תנא whose view on the open-ended alley appears in the ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about what the משנה means. The גמרא is saying the משנה clashes with both known opinions, so it needs to explain how that can be.

phrases.english: GEMARA: In accordance with whom?
For it is not like Chananya
and not like the first tanna.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כַּחֲנַנְיָה וְלָא כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה (Step 29) to the גמרא's first problem with it
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה of בית שמאי and בית הלל on fixing an alley
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה covers all alleys, then for an open-ended alley it allows a לחי and קורה. Both חנניה and the תנא קמא reject that, so the משנה matches neither of them.

steps.title: The משנה is only about a closed alley
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה is only discussing a מבוי סתום, an alley closed on one end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that this is what the משנה means: How is a closed alley made fit? בית שמאי say it needs a לחי and a קורה. בית הלל say it needs either a לחי or a קורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the problem. He reads the משנה as talking only about an alley that is closed on one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of חנניה and the תנא קמא dealt with an alley open on both ends. Once the משנה is limited to a closed alley, the two sources are about different cases, so there is no contradiction. The amounts that בית שמאי and בית הלל require are now only for the closed alley.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means, used when a source is being reread or clarified
Making something fit or permitted, here so that one may carry
An alley closed on one end and open to the public domain only on the other

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל is about a closed alley only. An alley open on both ends needs more.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is saying:
How is a closed alley made fit?
phrases.notes: רב יהודה adds the word סתום, 'closed,' to the משנה

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: a side post and a cross beam,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: either a side post or a cross beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covers every alley, including one open on both ends
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only a מבוי סתום, so it does not clash with the ברייתא

steps.title: Do בית שמאי hold that four walls are Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that since בית שמאי require both fixes, they must hold that a private domain needs four walls by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say a לחי and a קורה are needed. Does this mean בית שמאי hold that four walls are required by Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the reason behind בית שמאי's view. It suggests a conclusion and is setting up the next move, where that conclusion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A closed alley already has three walls. A לחי counts as a kind of partition for the open side. Since בית שמאי insist on a לחי, it looks as if they need a fourth wall, which would mean a רשות היחיד requires four walls מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? It introduces a suggested conclusion
Partitions or walls
By Torah law, as opposed to rabbinic law

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: a side post and a cross beam,
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה again in order to analyze it

phrases.english: is that to say that Beit Shammai hold:
four partitions are required by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading in Step 33 and asks what rule lies behind בית שמאי's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does בית שמאי's requirement show that they hold four walls are needed for a רשות היחיד by Torah law?

steps.title: Three walls create liability, but carrying needs four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Throwing in from outside is a Torah violation once there are three walls, but carrying inside is allowed only when there are four.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. For throwing, one is already liable once there are three walls. For carrying inside, it is not allowed until there are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from Step 34. בית שמאי's requirement does not prove what the Torah requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, three walls already make an area a רשות היחיד, so throwing into it from the public domain makes one חייב. Even so, the חכמים did not allow carrying inside until there are four walls. בית שמאי's demand for a לחי can come from that rabbinic rule about carrying, so it does not show that four walls are a Torah requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: To throw an object from one domain into another
He is liable
To carry or move objects within an area

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that the area stops being a רשות היחיד when it has only three walls. It is a Torah רשות היחיד for liability, and only permission to carry inside waits for four.
steps.whatToRemember: Three walls are enough for Torah liability. Four walls are needed before one may carry, so requiring a fourth wall does not prove what the Torah requires.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two questions: what makes one liable by Torah law, and what is required before carrying is permitted. This distinction comes up again and again in the laws of מבוי.

phrases.english: No,
to throw: from three walls one is liable,
to carry: not until there are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion suggested in Step 34
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that בית שמאי hold four walls are needed by Torah law
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It mixes up the rule for being allowed to carry, which needs four walls, with Torah liability, which begins at three walls

steps.title: Do בית הלל hold that three walls are a Torah requirement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית הלל, who need only a לחי or a קורה, and suggests this shows they hold that three walls make a private domain by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: either a side post or a crossbeam is enough. Shall we say that בית הלל hold that three walls are required by Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now runs the same test on בית הלל that it just ran on בית שמאי. It suggests that their lenient ruling reveals what they think the Torah requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל are satisfied with just one fix, either a לחי or a קורה. The suggestion is that they must hold that three walls already make a private domain by Torah law. If so, the single fix would only be an extra marker.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post placed at the open end of an alley
A crossbeam laid across the top of the alley's entrance
'Shall we say?' The opening of a suggested proof or inference
By Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic rule

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Beit Hillel say: either a side post or a crossbeam.
phrases.notes: The גמרא brings this line of the משנה back so it can draw a conclusion from it.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Beit Hillel hold
that three walls are required by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 34. The same type of inference is now made about בית הלל instead of בית שמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does בית הלל's need for just one fix show that they hold three walls make a private domain by Torah law?

steps.title: Throwing needs fewer walls than carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Throwing into the area is a Torah violation once there are two walls, but carrying inside is allowed only once there are three.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. For throwing, one is already liable once there are two walls. For carrying, it is not allowed until there are three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says בית הלל's ruling does not prove what the Torah requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different questions here. The first is when throwing into the area counts as a Torah violation, and two walls are already enough for that. The second is when one may carry inside, and the חכמים did not allow that until there are three walls. A closed מבוי already has those three walls, so בית הלל's single לחי or קורה is only a marker, and their ruling tells us nothing about the Torah minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: To throw an object from the public domain into a private domain
To carry or move an object within the area
Is liable for violating the Torah prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. The lower number of walls (two) applies to throwing in and being liable. The higher number (three) applies to being allowed to carry inside. Being 'private enough' to be liable for throwing in does not mean the area is 'private enough' to carry in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same move the גמרא used in Step 35. It separates the Torah definition that creates liability from the rule that permits carrying, so neither בית שמאי nor בית הלל can be used to prove the Torah minimum.

phrases.english: No. Regarding throwing in:
from two walls one is already liable;
regarding carrying: not until there are three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference proposed in Step 36.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that בית הלל's ruling reveals the Torah minimum of walls.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof mixed up the number of walls needed for liability when throwing (two) with the number needed to permit carrying (three).

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר require a crossbeam along with his two side posts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view that two side posts are needed. It then asks whether he means two side posts plus a crossbeam, or two side posts with no crossbeam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: two side posts. They asked: Does רבי אליעזר mean two side posts and a crossbeam, or perhaps two side posts without a crossbeam?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next opinion in the משנה, רבי אליעזר. It raises an open question about what exactly he requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's words 'two side posts' can be read in two ways. In the first reading he is stricter than בית שמאי, keeping their crossbeam and requiring two side posts instead of one. In the second reading the two side posts take the place of the crossbeam entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: Two side posts, the plural of לֶחִי
'It was asked of them.' The formula that opens a genuine open question
'Or perhaps.' It introduces the second possibility
Without

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: side posts.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The plural means two side posts.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Does Rabbi Eliezer mean side posts and a crossbeam,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא לְחָיַיִן בְּלֹא קוֹרָה קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: or perhaps he means side posts without a crossbeam?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of בית שמאי and בית הלל behind and opens a new question about רבי אליעזר's opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר's two side posts are in addition to a crossbeam or instead of one.

steps.title: A story about רבי אליעזר visiting his student
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins bringing a story about רבי אליעזר visiting his student רבי יוסי בן פרידא, to help settle the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There was an incident with רבי אליעזר, who went to his student רבי יוסי בן פרידא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by starting a story that will try to answer the question. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real event involving רבי אליעזר himself can show how he actually ruled. That would tell us which of the two readings of 'two side posts' is correct. The key details of the story come in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear.' It introduces a source brought to answer a question
An incident, a story of something that actually happened
His student

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָלַךְ אֵצֶל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן פְּרִידָא תַּלְמִידוֹ
phrases.english: who went to Rabbi Yosei ben Perida, his student,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer the question raised in Step 38.
steps.raayaObject: Which of the two readings of רבי אליעזר's 'two side posts' is correct.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story (from the תוספתא) about רבי אליעזר visiting his student רבי יוסי בן פרידא.
